item.description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism Peace of Mind with Modern Buddhism Teacher Kadam Sharon Lovich Peace is the foundation of our happiness and the good news is this potential for peace already exists within our own mind. In this relaxing series we will explore a variety of simple and practical meditations that will help us slow down, let go of stress and connect with our natural capacity for peace, happiness and a positive outlook. Each class focuses on a different meditation that you can easily bring into your daily life giving you practical tools to create a calmer and happier way of living. Everyone is welcome - no meditation experience required. Cost: $12 (free and online options for members) [Read More and Register](https://www.meditationinasheville.org/wednesday-drop-in-meditation-class-asheville-nc/) [Become a Member](https://www.meditationinasheville.org/become-a-member/)
Source: Meditation in Asheville

item.description:
UU Asheville Fiber Friends is a group of crafters who do handwork on personal projects and for the community. Mainly knitters and crocheters, we create warm items for donation to local charities (serving children, youth, and adults) and make a variety of cotton cloths given to Meals on Wheels for their “Santa for seniors” packages each December. A limited supply of yarn and tools (needles and hooks) are also available.
Join us the first Saturday of each month in the parlor of 23 Edwin, from 10 AM until about 12 noon. For more information or to be added to the monthly email reminder list, contact Mara Sprain.

item.title: Weekly Critique — Wed Nov 18, 6:00 PM
item.description:
AVL Writers This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.
For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.
Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.
If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.
If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).
Source: AVL Writers

item.title: Healthy Soil for Healthy Crops — Thu Dec 10, 1:00 PM
item.description: Healthy Soil for Healthy Crops with Mark Dempsey Thursday, December 10 | 1 pm – 4 pm BREG – Core Register Here! Come learn about how soil works and how to improve soil health. We will cover the basics of soil, the critical role of organic matter, how to sample soil and interpret a nutrient test, and what actions you can take to make your soil better. Drawing from research and on-farm experience, the class emphasizes practical, science-based strategies for improving soil health, reducing erosion, and building resilient farming systems. Mark Dempsey works with the Carolina Farm Stewardship Association as conservation specialist and soil health educator. His background includes more than 15 years of research and education in soil microbiology, no-till farming, cover crops, and sustainable agriculture systems. item.description:
Hailing from the Appalachian musical stronghold of Asheville, NC, The Nature Boys are coming in hot with their brand of bluegrass. As veterans of the acoustic music scene, they are combining a deep love of traditional string band music with a refreshing catalog of original songs, dazzling fans with a certain je ne sais quoi that is both genuine and relatable.
Formed in the summer of 2025, long time friends Jack, Jesse, and Nick found themselves once again living in the same town and ready to start a new musical project. These three had spent years touring across the world, often but not always in the same group. With a shared love of music, humor, and brotherhood, The Nature Boys was born in a way that can only be described as natural. Soon after getting the wheels rolling, they enlisted Asheville aces Coop and Korey, now forming one of Asheville’s premier 5-piece bluegrass bands, The Nature Boys.
